title: Loescher 2025 · Cardiac interoception and near/far PPS
citation: Loescher, M., Haggard, P., & Tallon-Baudry, C. (2025). Interoception vs. Exteroception: Cardiac interoception competes with tactile perception, yet also facilitates self-relevance encoding. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 122(49), e2516229122.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

published_method.apparatus: Place two fixed Visaton FRS 8 loudspeakers forward of the participant, less than 10 cm and 130 cm from the right hand. Stabilize the head in a chinrest and fix gaze past the far speaker.

tone.scope: The original WAV samples and software output request differ in rate. Delivered tone duration and spectrum depend on how the playback path handled the mismatch.

published_method.tactile_target: A 200 μs square electrocutaneous pulse delivered on the right hand dorsum with a Digitimer DS7A. Recheck twice-threshold intensity when changing electrode site after each block.
published_method.bimodal_timing: The task code commands sound 40 ms after the tactile trigger. The preprocessing re-creates touch onset 40 ms before the bimodal audio marker. Actual delivery follows hardware latency.
published_method.timing: Sample the pre-event delay uniformly from 4 to 8 s. Enter and exit each block with a 30 s physiological rest reference. The 1 s response window is anchored to the tactile command in tactile trials.
published_method.response: Right-index key press for tactile events, withheld on sound-only trials.
published_method.analysis: Classify trials by observed cardiac phase and relate heartbeat-evoked EEG and tactile reaction time to the fixed near/far contrast. The original analysis also evaluates somatosensory potentials, and applies heartbeat shuffles.
published_method.version: PNAS version of record. The task materials and 2025 preprint describe the acquisition lineage.

implementation_gaps: Deliver the original or validated stationary tone through two physical, calibrated output channels. Reconcile device rate with source rate and measure the near/far ear-level signals.
Synchronize the calibrated electrical pulse, two loudspeakers, key responses, EEG, ECG and fixation recording on the original timing contract. Reconcile TTL labels with the author event parser.

The acquisition path must support 4–8 s randomized pre-event timing, auditory-only catches, tactile-only controls and quiet physiological baselines. Validate physiological preprocessing and heartbeat-locked analyses on aligned records.
